name: 048_floor_grass_01.png
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Edit target: attached grass ground tile. The user says the existing texture is far TOO BUSY and the repeating pattern is obvious. Redesign it into an extremely restrained, nearly flat pixel-art grass texture for large tilemaps.
Keep the overall muted yellow-green color family, square top-down grass tile, opaque full-canvas surface. Final intended logical resolution 64x64; show crisp hard square pixels enlarged in a square image.
CRITICAL simplification: about 94-97 percent of the tile is ONE perfectly uniform base green, approximately #7DA34B. Only 3-6 percent consists of very tiny isolated one-pixel and occasional two-pixel grass marks. Use only two very close additional colors approximately #80A64E and #7AA049, nearly the same brightness as the base. The detail should be barely visible, quiet and low contrast even enlarged.
Distribute the tiny marks evenly and irregularly throughout the canvas with the same density in each area. No recognizable clumps, no connected large patches, no visual focal point, no diagonals or waves, no bright yellow specks, no blades taller than two logical pixels, no grass tuft icons, no dark islands. No large-scale color modulation, cloud noise, lighting gradient, vignette, directional shading, outlines or frame. No soil, rocks, flowers, props, text, grid or watermark.
The left/right and top/bottom edges must join smoothly in a seamless repeat. The result should look calm and practically uniform across an extended repeated floor; prevent any large repeating motif. Make the simplification unmistakable compared with the input. Variant A: a very sparse scatter of single pixels with just a few tiny horizontal two-pixel grass strokes.
